messages:
alice_support: customer-reported 5xxs and lots of p95 timeouts on hosted API. Request IDs: rq_3f9a2b, rq_3f9a2c. Getting repeated 504s from gateway, customer says it started ~15:10 UTC. Payloads are medium (approx 2k tokens).
ops-bot: ALERT: gateway_5xx_rate > 8% (5m) on prod-hosted-us-east. Link: https://grafana.internal/alerts/alerts/421 (incid-3281). :rotating_light:
bob_oncall: @alice_support can you paste a sample request (curl) and a short repro? Also check per-tenant queue depth at /dash/queue-depth for those request_ids.
alice_support: repro steps below. quick curl to the hosted API: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_cust_xxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"open-7b","input":"<~2k tokens~>","max_tokens":512}'
``` I ran it from us-east; returns 504 after ~12s.
carol_sre: looking at metrics now — continuous-batching queue depth spiked to ~720 concurrently, our cluster soft-limit is 512. Dequeue p95 increased from 30ms -> 1.8s, KV-cache miss rate jumped (spinups). Seeing many longseq requests (customer mixes long inputs + long max_tokens) which defeats batching.
dave_eng_runtime: short-term mitigation: set per-tenant early_reject when queue_depth > 600, reduce batch_window_ms to 8, and limit max_tokens per request for hosted tier. Example config snippet: ```yaml
routing:
  fallback_policy: accept_if_latency_ok
serving:
  batch_window_ms: 8
  early_reject_queue_depth: 600
``` Can ops flip a canary?
alice_support: trying quick change: hitting the admin toggle now to enable early_reject for tenant acme-inc (customer id). Running same curl after toggle...
alice_support: still 504, logs: ```json
{"ts":"2026-03-18T15:23:35Z","req_id":"rq_3f9a2b","error":"gateway_timeout","queue_depth":645,"dequeue_latency_ms":1820}
```
eve_support: (note) customer is on hosted (not dedicated) and on usage plan. No billing/auth anomalies in audit logs. Key looked fine.
bob_oncall: assigning Sev2 for now. @carol_sre @dave_eng_runtime please triage runbook step 1-3: validate queue_depth alarms, flip early_reject canary, apply fallback-model routing if capacity constrained.
carol_sre: did canary enable. Early-reject reduced tail-snowball for a subset but overall cluster still overloaded because many longseq requests were queuing and batchers holding KV state. I see eviction churn logs: `kvcache:spinup: tenant=acme-inc, misses=78` which slowed dequeues.
dave_eng_runtime: deployed a tiny routing change to send overflow requests to the lower-cost small-window variant (open-7b-compact) for a 10m window to relieve pressure. deploy-bot: Deployed routing change (commit f2a9d).
deploy-bot: @channel routing rollout 10% -> 100% in progress for acme-inc (f2a9d).
alice_support: after routing fallback, customer reports drop in 5xxs. p95 now back to ~420ms for that tenant. Still monitoring. :thumbsup:
carol_sre: root-cause hypothesis: a burst of long-sequence + large max_tokens requests created continuous-batching backlog; queue depth exceeded soft limits and KV cache spinups caused dequeue slowdowns -> gateway timeouts. Need longer-term fixes: tenant-aware batching windows, per-tenant sequencing limits, and better preload/eviction heuristics for KV cache.
dave_eng_runtime: agreed. Action items: (1) add per-tenant queue-depth quota enforcement + early_reject, (2) adaptive batch_window based on seq-length histograms, (3) tune kvcache prefetch for hot tenants. I'll open PRs.
bob_oncall: opened incident ticket INC-2026-3281, set priority P2, linking diagnostics: https://internal/incident/INC-2026-3281.
alice_support: documenting repro and what we did in the ticket. Will follow up with customer and post postmortem when RC confirmed. Thanks all for fast help.
carol_sre: recommended retrospective: add automated alert rule for "continuous-batcher queue depth > soft_limit and kvcache_miss_rate increase" to trigger early routing.
alice_support: noted. Closing this thread; continuing tracking in INC-2026-3281.
